features.title: Kotlin to Rust protocol seam
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone Watch app uses first-party frameworks; Open Crown's portable protocol logic is Rust behind a typed FFI.
features.notes: Verified on SM-A528B: libopencrown.so and JNA loaded; protocol revision and core rules rendered in Diagnostics.

features.title: Observation model
features.iphone_behavior: Every value the iPhone Watch app shows reflects a live watch state or a named cached state; nothing is shown as applied before the watch confirms it.
features.notes: Carries source, freshness, pair/epoch and confidence. UI must render unavailable states explicitly.

features.title: Feature registry
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone feature surface is organised by capability with a clear availability state.

features.title: Exact device profile matching
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone app is preinstalled; a third-party companion must decide whether its privileged payload matches the exact phone/kernel before acting.
features.notes: Host-tested exact model+kernel matching. The app must never hardcode an offset.

features.title: Signed payload verification
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable to a stock iPhone; required for any borrowed-privilege Android companion.

features.title: Read-only payload readiness
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable to a stock iPhone; shows whether a payload would be ready without executing it.

features.title: Borrowed-privilege payload execution
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable to a stock iPhone; Android needs a per-boot privileged process.
features.notes: The existing A52 chain is quarantined payload code with a provenance review open (PROVENANCE.md section 7).

features.title: uid 0 + controller-capable domain
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone owns the radio through its own frameworks; an Android companion must hold the controller itself.
features.notes: K2a. The A52 chain gives init-domain uid 0 but has not bound HCI_CHANNEL_USER under enforcing SELinux.

features.title: App-to-agent broker
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone Watch app talks to the watch through privileged first-party daemons.
features.notes: Measured: shell domain connects to @dfi_init, app-domain runas_app gets EACCES; the relay is unauthenticated raw-syscall root and never returns to init.

features.title: Authenticated agent IPC
features.iphone_behavior: First-party daemons use private authenticated IPC; a third-party agent must authenticate the app caller.

features.title: Resident agent lifecycle
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone has always-on daemons; the Android agent must be visible, watchdogged and gone at reboot.

features.title: Bluetooth controller ownership
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone Bluetooth stack is the controller owner and exposes link control to the Watch app.

features.title: BLE discovery and advertisement decoding
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone discovers a nearby Watch and shows it with model and pairing state.
features.notes: Android scanning is implemented, but FE25 setup-metadata decode is UNKNOWN, so no advertisement is selectable.

features.title: Unprivileged BLE observation
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone scans for nearby Apple advertisements; an observation alone is never a pairing candidate.
features.notes: Verified on SM-A528B in debug and in the release artifact: Apple advertisements listed, all Not selectable. Does not verify Watch detection or FE25 decode.

features.title: Discovery inventory and selection rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone bounds its candidate list, expires stale watches and rechecks a selection before connecting.
features.notes: Rust owns the inventory/tokens/TTL and the app renders them on hardware; selection success is unverified without FE25 metadata and a Watch.

features.title: BR/EDR + BLE link establishment
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone establishes the pairing and normal links automatically.

features.title: L2CAP / ERTM channels
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone opens the Watch protocol channels over L2CAP.

features.title: SMP / OOB security
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone completes Bluetooth security with out-of-band material during pairing.

features.title: Encrypted durable link
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone reconnects to a paired Watch with an encrypted link and no re-pairing.

features.title: NetworkRelay / ESP / IPsec
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone carries IP traffic to the Watch through NetworkRelay.

features.title: IDS application session
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone exchanges Watch application messages over IDS.
features.notes: Session rules are implemented separately; the IDS envelope and control Hello remain UNKNOWN.

features.title: Face mutation and read-back rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone applies a face change only after the Watch reports the expected collection; a timeout or disconnect is unknown, not applied.
features.notes: Complete-baseline planning, last-face refusal, exact reorder, staged transaction, 180 s read-back and 16 MiB/64 KiB limits. Wire encoding remains UNKNOWN.

features.title: Preference write baselines and read-back
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone confirms a Watch setting only after the exact key is observed with the new value.
features.notes: Known key/domain table, unknown-never-false, pair/session/revision baseline, exact-key read-back and timeout-is-unknown. NPS value encodings remain UNKNOWN.

features.title: Pigment sets and baseline
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone sends both complete pigment sets and confirms them from a new mirror.
features.notes: 1023 names/64 KiB bounds, duplicate/empty refusal, pair/session binding and exact two-set mirror confirmation. Palette namespace remains UNKNOWN.

features.title: Wi-Fi provisioning guards
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone dispatches one encrypted network archive per setup generation and never treats an ACK as a Wi-Fi join.
features.notes: WPA2-PSK/CCMP only, three reads five seconds apart, ten-second archive lifetime, one dispatch per generation and delivery-versus-join separation. Archive layout remains UNKNOWN; no passphrase is held by the guard.

features.title: Health defaults mirror rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone validates and merges Watch health defaults without turning missing data into zero.
features.notes: Newer-replaces/equal-or-older-ignored, tombstones keep the prior date, missing domain becomes empty, missing value never becomes zero, bounded 4096 rows/16 MiB, transactional batches. Encryption/anchors/native acceptance remain UNKNOWN.

features.title: Pairing branch and bond ordering rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone pairs through a PIN or optical branch, never both, and reports bonded only after SMP and durable storage succeed.
features.notes: Branch exclusivity, bounded PIN attempts, optical downgrade/MAC refusal, bond-store failure, replacement ordering and optical payload parsing. uIKE/SPAKE2+/SMP wire formats remain UNKNOWN.

features.title: Write-then-observe confirmation
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone shows a setting as changed only after the Watch reports the new value.
features.notes: Queued, sent, acknowledged, observed; stale epoch/target dropped, mismatch failed, timeout expired. ACK never applies. Host tests only.

features.title: Notification claim journal rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone applies a Watch action only to the exact notification revision it came from, and never twice.
features.notes: Revision-bound actions and replies, tombstone non-resurrection, terminal no-retry outcomes and 4 KiB content bound; bulletin encoding remains UNKNOWN.

features.title: Provisioning checkpoints and completion rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone reaches setup completion through activation, PairedSync and either a strict native barrier or an explicitly recorded owner confirmation.
features.notes: Ordered checkpoints, locale hard stop, ACK-is-not-completion, strict and owner-confirmed routes. PBBridge/NPS payloads remain UNKNOWN.

features.title: IDS route, epoch and reconnect rules
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone rejects unknown routes, drops replies from an earlier session and backs off between reconnect attempts.
features.notes: Route catalogue, class checks, epoch correlation, receipt-versus-effect split and 15/30/60 s backoff; no wire codec.

features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone uses the Watch feature services for settings, faces, health and apps.

features.title: Pair identity, epoch and replay protection

features.title: Stolen device support
features.iphone_behavior: No legitimate iPhone Watch feature supports operating a device the user does not own.

features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone shows authorised activity and location reports for a family member.

features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone applies contacts, communication and content restrictions.

features.title: Family Apple services

features.title: Privacy policy
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone Watch app links privacy information for Health and account data.
features.notes: Documented and rendered on the A52 with live permission state. Not a legal review.

features.title: Security notes
features.iphone_behavior: Not a stock iPhone screen; Open Crown documents its borrowed privilege and agent surface.
features.notes: Trust boundaries, secret handling, privileged payload quarantine and supply-chain gaps documented.

features.title: Evidence and blockers
features.iphone_behavior: Not a stock iPhone screen; Open Crown shows what is verified, what is unverified and what is blocked.
features.notes: Registry browser with filters, blocker detail and feature rows; physically exercised on the A52.

features.title: Open-source licences
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone Settings app shows software licences.
features.notes: Physical screen and inventory match. Licence texts and a release SBOM are explicitly still open gates.

features.title: Blocker transparency
features.iphone_behavior: No equivalent; the product must not hide blocked iPhone parity behind a generic error.
features.notes: Blocked rows name a catalog entry with dependency and reason in the app.

features.title: Clean-room similarity audit
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable to the iPhone app; required for this reimplementation.

features.title: Reference quarantine guard
features.iphone_behavior: No iPhone equivalent; keeps the quarantined reference out of tracked files and build inputs.

features.title: Licence audit
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable; required because the reference has no licence.

features.title: Secret and identifier scan
features.iphone_behavior: Not applicable; Open Crown must keep pairing keys and device identifiers out of logs and commits.
features.notes: Scans tracked text for private-key blocks, provider tokens and signing-material suffixes without echoing matches; wired into CI. Device serials are not pattern-scanned.

features.title: In-place app update
features.iphone_behavior: A companion must be updatable without losing local state or requiring a new pairing.
features.notes: Verified on the A52 with the same debug key: onboarding and per-app mute survived install -r, and a new muted notification was not captured. No pair record existed, so sealed-state preservation is not proven.

features.title: Watch backup
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone backs up Watch state so it can be restored.
features.notes: No backup format or consistency proof; destructive and untested.

features.title: Watch restore
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone restores a backed-up Watch identity and data.
features.notes: Requires a verified backup set first; no restore path exists.

features.title: watchOS update verification
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone verifies a watchOS update before installation.

features.title: Recovery drill
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone recovers from reboot, unpair, watch reset and app reinstall.
features.notes: App reinstall and reboot tested on the A52: onboarding reset, listener access absent, core loads. Watch unpair/reset and populated-store recovery are not testable without a Watch.

features.title: Release build and install path
features.iphone_behavior: The iPhone app ships through the App Store; Open Crown ships an APK with reproducible checks.
features.notes: R8 release starts and loads UniFFI on the A52. Environment-based signing and tools/release/verify-artifact.sh enforce signature, minSdk 33 and exclusion of the quarantined relay/payload; CI runs the gate with a throwaway key. Two clean builds at b0c62b0 were byte-identical. A runtime-only SBOM is generated; production key custody, SBOM signing/publication and distribution are not verified.

features.title: Fuzz and negative tests
features.iphone_behavior: Not user-visible; required for protocol robustness.
